timeline: Dr. Finch unlocks a hidden door in the wall with an iron key and leads Elara down a spiral stairway that descends into the mountain
Elara counts the steps: forty-seven, sixty-two, eighty-three
At the bottom, the stair opens into a vast cathedral-high cavity carved into the mountain, containing rows of glass-and-iron vats connected by thick black tubing
The vats hold a black fluid that swirls with visible, life-like movement
Finch stands beside a vat and calls the 'protein isolate' a useful fiction
Elara examines glass cases embedded in the stone walls: a preserved human arm split lengthwise to show black vascular channels replacing nerves and blood vessels
A charcoal drawing by Tobias hangs beside the arm, matching the anatomy exactly
A second glass case holds full-body transverse sections showing black structures in the spine, brainstem, and heart
A third case contains a diagram of the sanatorium with its tunnels drawn in the same branching pattern, converging on a single dark chamber marked with a salt symbol
Elara realizes the black fluid is living parasitic tissue from an organism beneath the mountain, and the therapy is designed to replace human wiring with this biomass
Finch confirms that the treatment is not for pain but to feed something
Elara speaks without shaking, out of anger
Dr. Finch orders Nurse Cora to prepare Elara for completion in the lower mineral room
The organism inside Elara responds to Finch's command with a wet pulse that is not her heartbeat
Elara's hidden salt under the bandage burns the black threads, causing them to flinch and restoring some normal sensation
The iridescent shimmer appears on the mineral walls, tracing seams and scratches to reveal an escape route away from the treatment frame
Finch explains that the final stage will make her whole and remove pain and loneliness
Elara refuses the final stage flatly, saying 'No'

knows: she is a pain patient receiving experimental therapy
the injection fluid is black and cold
Dr. Finch is the administering physician
Nurse Cora is the attending nurse
a young patient watched her from the doorway
the drawing shows her wrist with advanced black roots that match the injection
